items.title: JPMorgan Raises 2026 NII Outlook: What Does It Mean for Earnings?
items.summary: JPM lifts its 2026 NII outlook to $105.5B as loan and deposit growth offset rate pressures, though higher expenses may temper profit gains.

items.title: Bond Yields Are ‘Elephant in Room’ Stock Investors Are Ignoring
items.summary: If professional investors are worried that the rise in global bond yields will derail a bull market in stocks, you’d never guess it by looking at what they’re doing with the money they manage.

items.title: Bank of America sends message on Capital One stock
items.summary: Capital One’s July update showed slower card growth as Bank of America weighed the lender’s credit performance and outlook.

items.title: The 60/40 Portfolio Is ‘Broken.’ Here’s How to Fix It.
items.summary: A bond market selloff has pressured 60/40 investment portfolios, which have returned 8% on average this year compared with 13% for the S&P 500. Investors can look to healthcare stocks for relief.

items.title: Bank of America makes bullish call on 77-year-old healthcare stock
items.summary: The company is heading toward earnings with one growth engine still running hot, while Bank of America sees another potential catalyst building.

items.title: Why Workday (WDAY) Stock Is Trading Up Today
items.summary: Shares of enterprise software company Workday (NASDAQ:WDAY) jumped 4.5% in the afternoon session after Bank of America significantly raised its price target on the stock, while Barclays reiterated a positive rating, a TipRanks report revealed.

items.title: Which Big Bank Stock Has Dominated in 2026: Bank of America, Wells Fargo, or Bank of New York Mellon Corp.?
items.summary: Three big bank names have taken three wildly different paths through 2026, and the gap between the winner and the loser comes down to a business model difference that most investors overlook when picking financial stocks.

items.title: Software Stocks Are Bouncing Back From AI Fears. BofA Sees More Gains Ahead.
items.summary: Investors have become all too familiar with the fact that the software sector is under pressure as Wall Street worries about the impacts of artificial intelligence.  As AI models become more advanced, fears that those models will eventually replace critical software functions escalate.  Shares of creative software firm  Adobe  for example, have dropped 23% this year while shares of enterprise software company  ServiceNow  have fallen 17%.
